title: Linking to a Document Hosted Elsewhere
excerpt: When a source must remain on another service, the external-document template provides context and a clear outbound action without depending on iframe permissions.
body:
## Why use an external record?

Large files, institutional archives, or source-controlled repositories may need to remain outside the publication. This template keeps the article page stable while making the hosting boundary clear to readers.
author: editorial-team
document_description: The source is maintained outside this publication. The destination opens in a new browser tab.
seo_description: A safe external-document article template that does not assume iframe support.
editor_notes: Sample content reviewed for starter validation. Replace or remove before launch.
document_accessible_summary: This demonstration represents a document that remains on an external website. The article explains why a publisher may link to an outside archive, what readers should expect when following the link, and that the destination is controlled by a different service. The sample URL is a placeholder and may not host a real file.
document_accessibility_note: The HTML summary is provided so readers can understand the purpose and essential context without relying on the embedded PDF viewer.
methodology: This entry demonstrates how an editor can provide context and an accessible summary when the primary document is hosted on another website.
disclosure: The external URL is a neutral example address used for template testing.
rights_and_reuse: The linked publisher controls the external document and its reuse terms.
what_changed: Added a clearly labeled announcement classification and related coverage.
